title: Trading Policy

tiers.name: all directors and employees
tiers.description: All directors and employees of Capricorn Metals and its subsidiaries, and contractors of Capricorn Metals who are Restricted Persons. Bound by the insider trading prohibition, the ban on short-term trading, and any restricted trading period notified by the Company under 5.5, but not by the Closed Period regime unless they are Restricted Persons.

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: All directors and their spouses and related parties (as defined in the Corporations Act 2001), contractors notified in writing by the Chief Executive Officer or Company Secretary, and any person designated by the Chief Executive Officer as Key Management Personnel. Prohibited from dealing during Closed Periods without the permission of the Chairman or Company Secretary.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Directors of Capricorn Metals. Must seek approval from the Chairman or Company Secretary prior to any purchase or sale of securities, must complete a Trading Notification form within 2 days, are the subject of ASX notification within 5 business days, and are subject to the 3% cap on funding arrangements in 5.13.

tiers.name: Key Management Personnel
tiers.description: Any person designated by the Chief Executive Officer as key management personnel from time to time and notified in writing by the Company Secretary; likely to include those with authority and responsibility for planning, directing and controlling the activities of the Company and those involved in key financial, corporate or technical activities. Subject to the same pre-approval, notification and 3% funding cap as Directors.

tiers.name: spouses, dependents and related parties
tiers.description: Spouses (marriage or de facto), dependents under the age of eighteen, and related parties as defined in the Corporations Act 2001, including trusts of which a Restricted Person is trustee and beneficiary. The Policy applies equally to any dealings by them.

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The Company may at its discretion notify all Directors and employees that a restricted trading period is in effect, during which they must refrain from trading. No stated limit on duration and no statement about confidentiality of the reason. The Company Secretary separately notifies in writing those Key Management Personnel identified by the Chief Executive Officer as being affected by a Closed Period.

rules.detail: There is no derivatives rule as such. The Policy's scope provision applies it to derivatives and other financial products issued or created over or in respect of Capricorn securities, with no venue limitation, so an OTC put or call over Capricorn shares is within the Policy. Restricted Persons must not deal in them during Closed Periods without the permission of the Chairman or Company Secretary, and Directors and Key Management Personnel must seek approval before any purchase or sale.
rules.evidence: This Policy applies to the following securities: ... derivatives and other financial products issued or created over or in respect of Capricorn securities

rules.detail: Directors must obtain approval from the Chairman or Company Secretary before any purchase or sale of securities in the Company, and derivatives over Capricorn securities are securities to which the Policy applies. There is no outright prohibition on entering into option positions and no distinction by security state or venue.
rules.evidence: Key Management Personnel and Directors of the Company must seek approval from the Chairman or Company Secretary prior to any purchase or sale of securities in the Company.

rules.detail: The Policy contains no hedging clause of any kind. There is no definition of hedging, no reference to limiting economic risk, and no restriction on hedging unvested or holding-locked incentive securities; the equity plan rules themselves are not incorporated into this document.

Monetisation, prepaid forwards and equity swaps are not named. They are financial products created over or in respect of Capricorn securities and so fall within the Policy's scope, requiring permission during Closed Periods and, for Directors and Key Management Personnel, approval before any purchase or sale. If the structure involves funding security over the shares it is also subject to the 3% cap in 5.13.
rules.evidence: derivatives and other financial products issued or created over or in respect of Capricorn securities

rules.detail: Short selling is never mentioned. There is no prohibition on taking a position that profits from a decline in the Company's share price, and no economic-effect test of the kind found in most ASX trading policies.
Securities lending is not mentioned and there is no definition of dealing that would sweep it in; only buying, selling and trading are regulated.

CFDs are not named. A CFD over Capricorn securities is a financial product created in respect of those securities and so falls within the Policy's scope, requiring permission in Closed Periods and pre-approval for Directors and Key Management Personnel. In practice a CFD would also be caught by the ban on short-term trading in 5.6.
rules.evidence: Directors and employees should never engage in short-term trading of the Company's securities

rules.floor: the funding security must stay below the equivalent of 3% of the Company's listed shares
rules.detail: Margin lending is not named. A margin loan is a funding arrangement relating to a Director's interest in the Company's shares or options, so it is prohibited only where the funding security would affect the equivalent of 3% or more of the Company's listed shares. Below that threshold the Policy imposes no prohibition, no approval requirement and no disclosure obligation specific to the arrangement.
rules.evidence: All Directors and Key Management Personnel are prohibited from entering into funding arrangements relating to their interests in the Company's shares or options where the funding security would affect the equivalent of 3% or more of the Company's listed shares.

rules.detail: Key Management Personnel are subject to the same single quantitative limit as Directors; a margin loan is a funding arrangement relating to their interests in the Company's shares or options and is prohibited only above the 3% threshold.

rules.detail: The only encumbrance provision is the 3% cap on funding security. Granting security, a charge, lien or pledge is not itself defined as a dealing and is not otherwise regulated, so an encumbrance unconnected with a funding arrangement, or one within the 3% limit, is unrestricted by the Policy.

There is no requirement for company approval, no notification of the arrangement, no LVR or price-trigger guidance and no treatment of forced sales.

rules.detail: The funding arrangements clause is addressed only to Directors and Key Management Personnel; the Policy says nothing about secured financing by other employees or by contractors who are Restricted Persons.
A flat prohibition expressed as an exhortation, with no defined period and no test of intention, carved out only for the exercise of options where the shares will be sold shortly thereafter.

Other examples of “exceptional circumstances” include a transfer of shares required by family court order or other legal requirement.

financing.price_trigger_guidance: No LVR, buffer or price-trigger guidance. The single quantitative constraint is that the funding security must not affect the equivalent of 3% or more of the Company's listed shares, a test measured against the Company's issued capital rather than the individual's holding or the loan-to-value ratio.

external_documents: Employee share plan rules (referred to but not reproduced)
exemption_authority: The Chairman may waive the Closed Period and restricted trading period restrictions in paragraphs 5.4 to 5.5 in cases of severe financial hardship or other exceptional circumstances, but only where the Restricted Person demonstrates they hold no price sensitive information and satisfies the Chairman that the circumstances are exceptional and the proposed sale or disposal is the only reasonable course of action available; a Trading Exemption Request form must be submitted to the Company Secretary and clearance is given in writing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: All Directors and Key Management Personnel are prohibited from entering into funding arrangements relating to their interests in the Company's shares or options where the funding security would affect the equivalent of 3% or more of the Company's listed shares.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is the only restriction on the loan leg of a funded collar: secured financing over Capricorn shares is permitted outright provided the pledged parcel stays below 3% of the Company's listed shares, so the structure must be sized against issued capital and monitored for buy-backs or capital reductions that could push it through the threshold.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Policy contains no reference to hedging, limiting economic risk, short selling, securities lending, margin calls or forced sales.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Neither collar leg is prohibited by the trading policy itself, which is unusually permissive; the bank should instead diligence the equity plan rules and section 206J of the Corporations Act, which are not incorporated into this document.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Key Management Personnel and Directors of the Company must seek approval from the Chairman or Company Secretary prior to any purchase or sale of securities in the Company.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The approval requirement is not confined to Closed Periods, so entry, roll, reset and unwind of the collar each need the Chairman's or Company Secretary's prior approval, with no stated validity period, response time or revocation mechanism.

bespoke_clauses.clause: from the end of each quarter until the commencement of trading on the second business day after the Company's Quarterly Report is released; from four weeks prior to the release of the Company's full year and half year financial results until the second business day after the financial results are released.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: As a quarterly-reporting miner the Company is closed for the whole gap between each quarter end and its quarterly report, on top of the four-week pre-results windows, leaving only short and irregular execution windows for pricing a collar.

bespoke_clauses.topic: derivatives brought in by scope, not by rule
bespoke_clauses.clause: This Policy applies to the following securities: ... derivatives and other financial products issued or created over or in respect of Capricorn securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The OTC put and call are within the Policy's scope even though no clause addresses derivatives, so both legs are subject to the Closed Period and pre-approval regime but to no substantive prohibition.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Restricted Person must satisfy the Chairman that the circumstances are exceptional and that the proposed sale or disposal of the securities is the only reasonable course of action available to them.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: There is no route to execute any collar step inside a Closed Period for a voluntary financing transaction, since the waiver requires the disposal to be the only reasonable course of action.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Policy does not address margin calls, forced sales by a financier, or sales by a third party outside the executive's control.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Enforcement or physical settlement by the bank during a Closed Period is not expressly a breach, but nor is it expressly excluded, so the position should be documented with the Chairman in advance rather than assumed.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Reports of any breaches of the Policy will be forwarded to the Audit and Risk Management Committee. ... Strict compliance with the policy is a condition of employment.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Any mis-step in approving or disclosing the collar is escalated to a board committee and can be treated as a termination event, so the paper trail of approvals should be complete before execution.

summary: A funded collar is possible under this policy, which is unusually permissive. Nothing in it prohibits hedging, short selling, securities lending or derivatives; derivatives and financial products created over or in respect of Capricorn securities are simply brought within the Policy's scope, so both collar legs are treated as ordinary dealings. The single hard constraint on the loan leg is 5.13: a Director or Key Management Person may not enter into a funding arrangement over their Capricorn shares or options where the funding security would affect the equivalent of 3% or more of the Company's listed shares, so the collared parcel must be sized below that threshold against issued capital. Execution must be pre-approved by the Chairman or Company Secretary before any purchase or sale, must fall outside the Closed Periods (four weeks before the half and full year results, the whole period from each quarter end until two business days after the Quarterly Report, and 30 days before a disclosure document) and outside any discretionary restricted trading period, with a Trading Notification form to the Company Secretary within 2 days and ASX notification of a Director's change in relevant interest within 5 business days. The Policy is silent on margin calls and forced sales, so the bank's enforcement and settlement rights during a closed period should be agreed with the Chairman in advance.
